correctness.rationale: For k favored rim spins and t favored apices, the forced bond cost is at least max(0,2k-n)+tk. The k-breakpoints are 0, floor(n/2), ceil(n/2), n; for 0<x<=2 the mixed or all-favored apex lines at the positive breakpoints cost t(k-x) more than the nonfavored-apex line, and k=0 cannot beat -x floor(n/2) since floor(n/2)>=3. For 2<=x<=n the line n(1-x) bounds all competing lines by their endpoint gaps, with only k=n at x=n; that is a three-sector apex tie, and the greatest slope in magnitude takes over beyond n. The rim equality patterns have no extraneous nonfavored bond costs when counted as proper colorings after excluding the apex colors. On the odd rim at x=1, the two boundary k-sectors add, while at x=2 all independent nonfavored rim sets contribute 3*2^|R|+6. The cyclic independence transfer eigenvalues give both terms of D_n; near activity 2 the top eigenvalue gives density 1/3 for R and variance O(n), so the limiting favored fraction is 2/3. At x=0 proper colorings are counted by whether apices coincide; x=n gives 4^2 apex choices. No unsupported finite-temperature inference is needed.
residual_risks: The replay is finite; the analytic inequalities and equality counting, rather than that replay, support the all-size quantifier.
